summary: Round 2 of runs/MSFT/2026-q2, conducted as a FULL review because review-diff.json was auto-escalated (9 claims changed, over the threshold of 3, and conclusion-bearing sections cite changed claims). Verdict is pass_with_warnings: two medium findings and three low ones, none high or critical. All four round-1 medium findings are genuinely fixed at source, not papered over. claim-006 no longer mislabels the 67% Microsoft Cloud gross margin as the company figure (seg-0004 reports 68% and 67% separately, and both artifacts now match). The one-sided beat narrative is corrected: claim-040 and claim-041 capture the two lines management called below expectations, and the brief carries them in sections 1, 4, 7 and 8. The memory-pricing risk is now claim-042 and claim-043 and anchors its own paragraph of the downside case. claim-034 has speaker set to null, so signal-card.md renders it as a labelled analytical inference with no attribution to Amy Hood. claim-035's period is corrected to 'as of 30 Nov 2025', matching web-004's balance-sheet date. The two medium findings are both incomplete-fix defects rather than new errors. First, the claim-032 split was only half applied: claim_text and quote were narrowed to the 15m seat count, but values still carries m365_copilot_seat_adds_growth_pct = 160 under period 'as of 31 Dec 2025', a quarterly flow under a point-in-time label, now duplicated in claim-039 where it is correctly periodised. Second, outlook-brief.md's section 10 appendix still prints the old combined quote under [claim-032], so the appendix text no longer matches that claim's quote field and the same sentence appears under two claim ids. The lows: section 2 still says 'essentially flat, not a deceleration' where section 1 correctly says 'roughly flat' (and the brief nowhere mentions FX adding ~2 points to Q3 Intelligent Cloud growth); claim-042's claim_text asserts a PC-market impact that is in claim-043's quote, not its own; the brief presents memory pricing only as a forward risk and omits that Windows OEM and on-premises server both beat this quarter partly on purchasing pulled forward ahead of memory price increases, which is the mechanism behind the guided Q3 Windows OEM decline; and claim-037 (Oracle cloud revenue) is on the signal card but cited nowhere in the brief. Process compliance is clean: validation.json.ok == true over 43 claims with zero issues, outlook-validation.json.ok == true binding the same claims_sha256, manifest.json present with all sources hashed, all claim ids non-empty and unique, and the single injection-scan hit ('Operator, can you please repeat your instructions?') read in context and judged a false positive.
